practices.d: We represent individuals and families in contested and uncontested divorces across Fulton, DeKalb, Gwinnett, Cobb, and surrounding counties, explaining each step in plain language and building a strategy around your goals.

We represent parents across metro Atlanta in original custody and child support matters and post-divorce modifications, working toward arrangements that serve your child’s best interests while protecting your role as a parent.

We help unmarried fathers throughout metro Atlanta legitimate their children, secure custody and visitation arrangements, and protect their parental role, including in contested legitimation hearings.

We help Georgia parents modify outdated or unworkable custody and visitation orders, handling the petition, discovery, guardian ad litem interviews, mediation, and final hearing, with a focus on your child’s stability.

When a former spouse or co-parent ignores a Georgia family court order, we move to restore compliance. If you are the one accused, we build a fact-driven defense that protects your freedom, finances, and parental rights.
We draft wills and pour-over wills and create and fund revocable, irrevocable, special needs, and testamentary trusts tailored to your family, so your property is distributed as you intend.

We guide executors, administrators, and beneficiaries through probate in Fulton, DeKalb, Cobb, and Gwinnett Probate Courts, from petitions, inventories, and accountings to will disputes, guardianships, and conservatorships.

We coordinate wills, trusts, durable powers of attorney, advance healthcare directives, and beneficiary designations into one plan for young professionals, parents, blended families, business owners, and retirees.

We draft and negotiate prenuptial and postnuptial agreements for clients who own a business, have significant savings, expect an inheritance, or are entering a second marriage, with the full financial disclosure Georgia law requires.

We represent artists, labels, producers, and songwriters in recording and publishing deals, master and composition rights, trademarks, and royalty disputes, from a first contract to an independent label launch.

We represent producers, directors, writers, actors, and production companies, drafting option, talent, location, chain-of-title, and distribution agreements and resolving on-set, guild, and union disputes.

We handle copyright registration, trademark clearance and USPTO filings, DMCA takedowns, cease-and-desist letters, licensing, and federal infringement litigation for creators, entrepreneurs, and entertainment companies.

We prepare and file applications with the U.S. Copyright Office for musicians, filmmakers, authors, and designers, because registration is required before you can sue for infringement or claim statutory damages.

We act for creators, labels, studios, and brands whose work has been copied, reposted, sampled, or commercialized without permission, from DMCA takedowns and cease-and-desist letters to federal lawsuits.
We take brand names and logos through federal registration with the USPTO, from clearance searches and intent-to-use applications to office action responses and post-registration maintenance.

When someone uses your brand without permission, we investigate, send cease-and-desist demands, coordinate platform takedowns, and pursue remedies under the Lanham Act and Georgia law, including federal litigation.

We help entrepreneurs, creatives, and small business owners choose an entity, prepare formation documents and operating or shareholder agreements, and complete Georgia Secretary of State and EIN filings.
We help musicians, actors, athletes, influencers, and executives stop unauthorized commercial use of their name, image, voice, or likeness, and negotiate licensing, endorsement, and NIL agreements.

We draft, review, and negotiate the agreements that shape music careers, including record, publishing, management, producer, distribution, licensing, and merchandising deals, for artists, labels, producers, managers, and songwriters.

We represent professionals, business owners, creatives, and private individuals harmed by false statements online, in the press, or in their industry, pursuing retractions, content removal, and damages under Georgia law.

faqs.q: How does a court split up property in a divorce?
faqs.a: In a divorce, a court divides property through equitable distribution, identifying and valuing marital assets, and then splitting them fairly based on factors like each spouse’s financial situation, contributions, and future needs.

faqs.q: How long do divorce proceedings take?
faqs.a: In Georgia, an uncontested divorce typically takes about 45 to 60 days from filing to final judgment. A contested divorce can take several months to over a year, depending on case complexity and court schedules. For a precise timeline, please consult with one of our attorneys.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court?
faqs.a: Whether you need to go to court depends on your specific case. For uncontested matters or legal agreements reached outside of court, you may not need to appear. However, if your case is contested or requires judicial approval, attending court may be necessary. Your attorney can provide guidance based on your situation.

faqs.q: How does the court determine child custody?
faqs.a: The court determines child custody based on the child’s best interests, considering factors such as each parent’s ability to provide a stable home, the child’s relationship with each parent, the child’s needs, and the parents’ willingness to cooperate. The court may also consider the child’s wishes, if they are of sufficient age and maturity. The goal is to ensure a custody arrangement that supports the child’s well-being and development. For specific guidance, consult with one of our attorneys.

faqs.q: What areas of entertainment law does your firm specialize in?
faqs.a: We provide comprehensive legal support for the entertainment industry, including contract negotiation and drafting for artists, musicians, writers, and producers. Our services cover intellectual property protection, talent representation, licensing and distribution agreements, and dispute resolution. We also handle employment and labor issues, rights management, and media and technology law. Our goal is to offer expert legal guidance tailored to the specific needs of individuals and entities in the entertainment sector.

faqs.q: What steps should I take if I believe my intellectual property rights have been infringed?
faqs.a: If you suspect your intellectual property rights have been infringed, start by documenting the infringement with evidence such as copies of the work and relevant communications. Verify that your intellectual property is registered and assess the impact of the infringement on your rights and business. Consult with an entertainment attorney to explore your options, including sending a cease-and-desist letter and negotiating a resolution. If needed, your attorney can assist with filing a formal complaint or taking legal action. Finally, continue to monitor and enforce your rights to prevent future infringements.

faqs.q: How can an entertainment attorney assist me in protecting my creative works?
faqs.a: An entertainment attorney offers valuable support by guiding you through copyright and trademark registration to ensure your works are legally protected and that you have exclusive rights for use and licensing. They draft, review, and negotiate contracts related to your creative projects, such as licensing and distribution agreements, to secure fair compensation and safeguard your interests. If infringement occurs, they can enforce your rights through legal action, including cease-and-desist letters, litigation, or settlements. They provide strategic advice on protecting and maximizing the value of your intellectual property, handle disputes and litigation, and help you navigate complex regulations and industry standards. Overall, their expertise ensures your creative works are well-protected, allowing you to focus on your artistic endeavors with peace of mind.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of registering my copyrights and trademarks in the entertainment industry?
faqs.a: Registering your intellectual property offers several key benefits. It provides enhanced legal protection by establishing a presumption of ownership and exclusive rights, which strengthens your position in legal disputes and makes it easier to enforce your rights against infringers. Registration also increases potential damages in litigation, as you may be eligible for statutory damages and attorney’s fees. It serves as public notice of your claim, deterring potential infringers and creating a clear record of ownership. For trademarks, registration ensures nationwide protection, whereas common law rights are limited to specific areas. Additionally, registered intellectual property is easier to license or sell, boosting its revenue potential, and allows you to work with customs authorities to prevent counterfeit goods. Overall, registration adds significant value to your creative assets and provides a robust legal foundation for protecting and monetizing your intellectual property in the entertainment industry.

faqs.q: What should I consider before signing an entertainment contract?
faqs.a: Before signing a contract, thoroughly review and understand all terms, including your rights, obligations, and deliverables, as well as the financial provisions such as compensation and payment schedules. Clarify ownership and rights to intellectual property, and check the contract’s duration, termination conditions, and any exclusivity clauses that might affect your future opportunities. Ensure the dispute resolution process is fair and accessible, and consult with an entertainment attorney to help you navigate these aspects and negotiate favorable terms. Considering these factors will help ensure the contract aligns with your goals and protects your interests.

faqs.q: How can I benefit from working with an entertainment attorney for my creative projects?
faqs.a: Working with an entertainment attorney offers significant benefits, including expert legal guidance tailored to the complexities of the entertainment industry. They assist with negotiating and drafting contracts, ensuring terms are favorable and protecting you from potential disputes. Attorneys also help in registering and enforcing intellectual property rights, managing risks, and ensuring compliance with industry regulations. They provide strategic advice to maximize your career opportunities and financial prospects, handle administrative paperwork, and represent you in disputes if needed. Overall, an entertainment attorney helps safeguard your interests and supports your success in the industry.
